title: Palomar transients missing in Earth's shadow
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Palomar transients missing in Earth's shadow, about 1949-1957 at Palomar Observatory, San Diego, California, and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote:
said, "Yeah, you know, these objects
are falling on the dark side of the Earth
when they shouldn't be being
illuminated by the sun?"

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about the VASCO project, studies of old sky photographs taken at Palomar Observatory in California between 1949 and 1957, and a researcher he names as Beatrice Valale. The studies found brief points of light, called transients, in those photos, and the story says they go missing in the part of the sky inside Earth's shadow, where sunlight cannot reach. If true, it would suggest the lights were sunlight bouncing off real objects high above Earth.
